editorial:
Imagine your band is failing and then you find a zombie who can scream like a death metal god. That is exactly what happens to Kana. She decides to recruit Tetsuo, the very same undead creature that ate her old bandmates, just to get famous. It sounds totally insane, and that is why it works. The movie has a wild, colorful energy that feels like a fever dream. You get a mix of gross-out gore and silly jokes that keep you guessing what weird thing will happen next. It does not take itself seriously at all, which makes the ride a lot of fun.

The acting is over-the-top in the best way possible, and the pacing never lets up. While some of the special effects look a bit cheap, it actually adds to the charm of the movie. If you love movies that are completely off the wall, you need to see this one. You should definitely try to find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best colors, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a big collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great move for those bonus features.
endingExplained: In the end, the government agents finally catch up to the band to take their zombie experiment back. However, the chaos peaks during a massive concert. Tetsuo and the band manage to outsmart the agents through a series of loud, messy battles. Instead of a sad ending, the movie wraps up with the band embracing their weirdness. They stay together, proving that fame is possible even if your lead singer is technically a rotting corpse.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird Japanese cinema and dark humor.
